reasoning_traces.think:
The core of game theory lies in modeling rational decision-making under uncertainty. Expected utility theory provides a cardinal representation of preferences that allows for risk analysis. Mixed strategies extend this to situations where deterministic choices fail, enabling Nash equilibria in games without pure strategy solutions. Common knowledge of rationality introduces a meta-level constraint on beliefs, ensuring consistent reasoning across players. These primitives form a layered structure: utility functions define value, mixed strategies enable equilibrium computation, and common knowledge ensures logical consistency among agents. Each layer builds upon the previous one, creating a robust foundation for Bayesian inference in GSI and situational logic in GSE.
